neighbours.label: the verb before 'around' in going around an obstacle instead of dealing with it ('simply walked around it', 'work around them')
fire: Rather than clear the fallen tree, the hikers just stepped around it.
Instead of repairing the pothole, drivers simply steered around it.
The team chose to code around the bug rather than fix it.
When the gate was locked, they climbed around the fence.
Rather than confront the issue, the board talked around it for an hour.
Unable to move the boulder, the villagers just walked around it.
She found a way to work around the broken scanner.
Instead of removing the stump, the gardener mowed around it.
quiet: Rather than leave the fallen tree, the hikers cut it into logs.
Instead of ignoring the pothole, the city repaired it quickly.
The team chose to fix the bug rather than hide it.
When the gate was locked, they waited for the guard.
Rather than ignore the issue, the board voted on it in an hour.
Unable to move the boulder, the villagers called a crane.
She found a way to repair the broken scanner.
Instead of mowing the lawn, the gardener weeded the beds.

notes: Card: + pole peaks on ' to' x15, 'walked' (around it), 'work' (around them), 'who'; logit effect suppresses skip/bypass/avoid. Probe: 'walked around it' 0.10-0.18, 'work around' 0.03, 'in order to' 0.07-0.10. Weak; best guess recorded as unclear.
